question: What is the correct sequence for a physical abdominal assessment?
explanation: Auscultation is performed before touching the abdomen so that manipulation does not alter natural bowel sounds. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T13#GNS213_U3_T13_h1)

question: Why must a nurse listen for a full five minutes before documenting absent bowel sounds?

options.A: Stethoscope tubing requires time to warm up to body temperature
options.B: Peristalsis can be sluggish and bowel sounds may be extremely infrequent
options.C: Hospital protocol mandates a prolonged listening period for legal records
options.D: Gastric acid production fluctuates in cycles lasting exactly five minutes

explanation: True absence of bowel motility must be verified patiently because sluggish sounds can easily be missed during a quick check. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T13#GNS213_U3_T13_h1)

question: Which electrolyte imbalance is most commonly triggered by severe vomiting and diarrhea?
explanation: Gastric and intestinal fluids contain high concentrations of potassium, which are rapidly depleted during prolonged vomiting or diarrhea. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T13#GNS213_U3_T13_h2)

question: A patient with severe gastroenteritis is receiving intravenous fluid therapy. What is the most reliable daily indicator of their fluid balance status?

options.A: Color and clarity of the urine

explanation: Daily weights provide an objective, quantifiable metric for tracking rapid fluid gains or losses over time. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T13#GNS213_U3_T13_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of introducing clear liquids as the first step in oral feeding advancement?

options.A: To supply the entire daily caloric requirement immediately
options.B: To permanently replace enteral tube feeding methods
options.C: To prevent electrolyte shifts by providing high sodium loads
options.D: To test gastrointestinal tolerance with minimal digestive residue

explanation: Clear liquids pass through the GI tract easily and let the clinician evaluate whether nausea or cramping returns before advancing. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T13#GNS213_U3_T13_h3)

question: A postoperative patient has advanced from clear liquids to full liquids and now reports mild nausea and abdominal cramping. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Immediately insert a nasogastric tube for continuous decompression
options.B: Force the patient to finish the meal to maintain nutritional schedules
options.C: Discontinue all monitoring because minor cramping is expected
options.D: Temporarily step back the diet to the previous tolerated level and notify the team

explanation: Cramping indicates the gut is not yet ready for the current dietary load, so pausing progression prevents worsening complications. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T13#GNS213_U3_T13_h3)

question: How do proton pump inhibitors exert their therapeutic effect in the stomach?

options.A: By inhibiting the hydrogen-potassium ATPase enzyme system
options.B: By forming a physical protective barrier over mucosal ulcers
options.C: By directly neutralizing existing hydrochloric acid in the lumen
options.D: By paralyzing local smooth muscle to stop gastric contractions

explanation: Proton pump inhibitors block the final step of acid production in the parietal cells, effectively lowering gastric acidity. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T13#GNS213_U3_T13_h4)

question: Why is flushing an enteral feeding tube before and after medication administration critical?

options.A: To cool down the medication temperature before it reaches the stomach
options.B: To prevent viscous medications from clogging the narrow tube lumen
options.C: To stimulate immediate gastric emptying and digestion of the drug
options.D: To hydrate the patient systemically through the gastrointestinal mucosa

explanation: Tube blockages interrupt nutrition and drug delivery, requiring costly and invasive tube replacement procedures. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T13#GNS213_U3_T13_h4)

question: Which clinical sign best indicates the resolution of a postoperative paralytic ileus?
explanation: The resumption of flatulence or bowel movements proves that coordinated peristalsis has returned to the gastrointestinal tract. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T13#GNS213_U3_T13_h5)

question: What is the primary rationale for encouraging early ambulation in patients recovering from abdominal surgery?

options.A: To immediately restore preoperative muscle strength and endurance
options.B: To accelerate the complete closure of superficial skin sutures
options.C: To stimulate peristalsis and reduce the risk of venous thromboembolism
options.D: To decrease the need for prescribed systemic pain medications

explanation: Movement encourages bowel motility and enhances circulation, helping prevent dangerous blood clots in the lower extremities. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T13#GNS213_U3_T13_h5)

question: Which physical finding is most characteristic of gastrointestinal perforation and peritonitis?
explanation: Peritoneal irritation from leaking bowel contents causes involuntary guarding and rigidity of the abdominal wall musculature. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T13#GNS213_U3_T13_h6)

question: What is the initial hemodynamic indicator of internal gastrointestinal bleeding?
explanation: The body compensates for lost intravascular volume by increasing the heart rate to maintain cardiac output before blood pressure drops. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T13#GNS213_U3_T13_h6)

question: When is the best time to begin patient education regarding stoma care after bowel surgery?

options.A: Immediately on the morning of planned hospital discharge
options.B: After the patient experiences their first complication at home
options.C: Early in the hospital stay with gradual hands-on practice
options.D: Exclusively through written pamphlets given at the bedside

explanation: Early introduction and repetitive practice build patient competence and reduce anxiety before leaving the controlled hospital environment. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T13#GNS213_U3_T13_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a warning sign that a recovering gastrointestinal patient should report immediately? (SELECT ONE)

options.A: Fresh bright red blood in the stool
options.D: Mild, passing gas with normal bowel movements

explanation: Passing gas indicates normal return of bowel function, whereas severe pain, bleeding, and fever are dangerous red flags. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T13#GNS213_U3_T13_h7)
